Based on their recent conversation history, XM has been working on multiple sophisticated AI and machine learning projects over the past few days. Their most recent completed work includes a Neo4j relationship-based neighbor retrieval system featuring a RelationshipBasedNeighborFetcher class that handles three relationship types (包含, 关联, 前后序) with BFS traversal logic and depth-limited traversal capabilities. Prior projects included a law firm web scraping system using Selenium with ThreadPoolExecutor concurrency, a modular prompt builder with pluggable architecture achieving 61.6% token reduction, and a comprehensive RAG evaluation pipeline spanning 10 modules and 5000+ lines of code comparing vector versus LLM-based retrieval methods.

XM also completed an LLM-as-Judge evaluation report analyzing a hybrid RAGFlow and Neo4j system across 39 QA pairs, finding Neo4j achieved 89.74% Hit@3 compared to RAGFlow's 20.51%. Additional completed work included RAGFlow and Neo4j chunking alignment analysis with four different alignment strategies, JSON file merging scripts, and an ArkUI layout QA dataset with 55 QA pairs mapped to both neo4j and ragflow chunk_ids. XM demonstrates expertise in knowledge graphs, retrieval systems, web scraping, and evaluation methodologies, working with Chinese language content and technical documentation. Claude provided a comprehensive summary of all completed projects and asked XM to specify which project needed continuation or if they wanted to start a new task.
